children: Conceptualised by Bare Bones Collective and executed by MOMS Outdoor, the Carter Road activation drew more than 5,000 participants and recorded over 10,000 attempts across two days

bigbasket has taken its Ganesh Chaturthi engagement on-ground with the Modak Meter, an interactive installation at Mumbai’s Carter Road that turned the familiar Ganpati Bappa Morya chant into a participatory brand experience.
Over two days, more than 5,000 people engaged with the activation, generating over 10,000 attempts on the sound meter. The highest recorded volume reached 120 decibels, according to the brand.

The centrepiece was a life-sized modak-shaped sound meter that invited visitors to shout Ganpati Bappa Morya and see how high they could take the reading. Participants crossing the 90-decibel mark received curated bigbasket goodie bags containing products from brands including Wow!, Open Secret, Tata Coffee, Ching’s Secret, Tetley, Bagrry’s, Wagh Bakri, Nissin and Plum.

The activation was built around a familiar behavioural cue from Mumbai’s Ganesh Chaturthi celebrations. Rather than introducing a new interaction, bigbasket used a chant already embedded in the festival to create a simple challenge that visitors could understand and participate in immediately.

The installation also developed a social dimension as crowds gathered around participants, cheering them on and watching subsequent attempts. According to bigbasket, around 30 per cent of participants crossed the threshold to receive the goodie bags, while some visitors returned to try to improve their earlier scores.

“Ganesh Chaturthi in Mumbai has an energy of its own, and the sound of ‘Ganpati Bappa Morya!’ is one of the most recognisable parts of that celebration. We wanted to build an experience around something people already know and naturally participate in. The Modak Meter gave them a simple way to bring that enthusiasm to life, while the response from the crowds made the activation even more engaging. It was particularly interesting to see people cheering for participants they had never met and coming back to try and beat their own scores,” says Arpit Jaiswal, Chief Growth Officer, bigbasket.

The Modak Meter formed part of bigbasket’s wider Ganesh Chaturthi campaign, which also brought the platform’s festive assortment into the campaign narrative. Consumers could access categories including puja essentials, modak ingredients, sweets, fruits and flowers through the platform.

The activation was conceptualised by Bare Bones Collective and executed by MOMS Outdoor, extending bigbasket’s festive presence from the digital shopping environment into a physical consumer experience.

The choice of an interactive OOH format also places the campaign within a broader shift towards festive brand activations that use participation rather than passive visibility to create engagement. In this case, the brand connected its grocery and festive-shopping proposition with a culturally familiar moment, turning a chant associated with Ganesh Chaturthi into the central mechanic of the experience.
